predecessors.name: Kingdom of Butua
predecessors.text: Butua's land: 'Certainly by his death in 1696, Changamire controlled all of Butua's territory'

successors.name: Ndebele Kingdom
successors.text: Matabeleland and the Midlands: 'conquered and subdued around 1838 by Mzilikazi's Ndebele' (Danamombe was 'destroyed in the 1830s when the Matabele arrived')

ledger.x: c. 1683: Changamire Dombo founds the Rozvi Empire on the Zimbabwean Plateau. 'The Rozvi Empire (c. 1683-1866) was a Shona state established by Changamire Dombo on the Zimbabwean Plateau.'
c. 1683: Dombo conquers Butua. 'Dombo defeated the Portuguese and Mutapa in battle before turning south to conquer Butua c. 1683.'
1695: Dombo's forces take Mutapa's gold-producing plateau.
c. 1712: 'the Changamire placed a Rozvi official in his zimbabwe and imposed conditions of vassalage' on the Mwenemutapa.
c. 1760: the Mutapa state 'disintegrated into principalities'; the page does not date the end of the Rozvi vassalage, so the year is a bridge to the Mutapa dossier's 1760 split.

c. 1838: Mzilikazi's Ndebele conquer the Rozvi heartland. 'it was invaded by no less than six groups which had fled during the Mfecane... until it was conquered and subdued around 1838 by Mzilikazi's Ndebele.' The region is the researcher's reading: Matabeleland and the Midlands, where Danamombe was 'destroyed in the…

c. 1838: the rest of the plateau passes out of Rozvi control into Shona chiefdoms (Tohwechipi 'fled to the Mavangwe Hills on the upper Save Valley' by 1857 and 'surrendered after a lengthy siege in 1866'). Page silent on which polity held it.
c. 1838: the Rozvi state ends under the Ndebele conquest. The infobox runs it to 1866 ('Surrender of Tohwechipi: 1866'), when the last Rozvi ruler gave up.

wars.name: Changamire Dombo's wars against Mutapa and the Portuguese
wars.outcome: 1693 Dambarare feira attacked; 1694 campaigning in Maungwe; 1695 Manyika invaded 'forcing the temporary abandonment of its feiras'; Dombo died c.

wars.name: Nguni invasions of the Rozvi state (Mfecane)
wars.outcome: 'throughout the 1830s it was invaded by no less than six groups which had fled during the Mfecane': Mpanga's Sotho repelled in 1832; Zwangendaba's Ngoni 'entered the state and wreaked devastation' in 1833 and left in 1835; Chirisamhuru killed c.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the extent is the plateau state and its tributary reach.
